topics: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private deployment tradeoffs
transcript:
Header: 2026-03-19 10:00 PDT | Duration: 57 min | Recording: yes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Samir Rao (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (Redwood Partnerships); Ravi Patel (Vellum Head of Platform), Nora Jennings (Vellum Dir Partnerships), Marcus Lee (Vellum CTO)

[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for carving time. Quick agenda, we'll run through the partner pipeline, pick three prioritized pilots, and align on technical next steps. Samir's gonna cover perf asks.
[00:12] Nora Jennings: Quick note — super excited, we had good interest internally after the exec brief. A few questions about pricing and security were flagged.
[00:18] Maya Chen: Great, we'll cover both. Samir, want to kick perf?
[00:22] Samir Rao: Yeah, sure. Hi all — quick context, we're focused on throughput and tail latency for your real-time summarization flow. You mentioned 8k average but spikes to 24-32k for multi-doc synthesis, right, Ravi?
[00:36] Ravi Patel: Yeah that's right, average 6–9k, spikes from user sessions combined across pipelines push it up. We also have a nightly batch that needs 32k context to stitch records.
[00:47] Samir Rao: Okay so the ask is: baseline hosted (Redwood hosted API), Dedicated (reserved pool), and Private (VPC) for the 8k/32k patterns to measure latency, cost per 1k tokens, and tail p95/p99. We'll also show batching and KV-cache benefits.
[01:05] Marcus Lee: What's the timeline for those benchmarks? We need numbers before the internal procurement in early April.
[01:10] Maya Chen: We're targeting a week turnaround for an initial perf spreadsheet. Samir, can you do a 7-day turnaround?
[01:15] Samir Rao: Yes, I can do an initial run with hosted vs dedicated profiles by next Thursday, 3/26. For private it'll need a short snapshot or architecture notes — we can model cost but we'd want a small on-prem POC to be precise.
[01:27] Nora Jennings: Also, how do you handle KV cache across requests? We worry about cold-starts impacting UX.
[01:33] Samir Rao: Good point. Redwood supports persistent KV cache for pinned sessions in Dedicated and Private. Hosted has a cache layer too; we can pin prefix caching per user session. Cold starts on first request look like a higher latency, but with warm caching p95 improves a lot. I'll include a cold vs warm run.
[01:50] Ravi Patel: Security — we have to check SOC2 and KMS integration. Which artifacts do you provide?
[01:55] Maya Chen: We have an enterprise security pack: SOC2 Type II report, ISO attestation (if needed), and we support KMS integrations for Private and Dedicated. For hosted, we offer customer-managed keys through our enterprise key wrapping. I'll attach the security pack after the call.
[02:10] Marcus Lee: Data residency? One of our pilot customers requires EU-only processing.
[02:14] Lena Ortiz: We can route to EU hosted regions or spin a VPC in their region for Private. There are some lead times for private deployments — typically 4–6 weeks depending on network.
[02:27] Nora Jennings: Hmm 4–6 weeks is long but ok if we can start a hosted pilot with assurances and SLA.
[02:33] Maya Chen: We can do a staged approach: hosted pilot for the initial two weeks while we scope Private. That gives you data to evaluate UX and a path to Private for residency.
[02:44] Samir Rao: For SLA, we offer dedicated pool SLAs for latency and uptime; hosted has standard SLOs but we can include a canary model routing and fallback for critical paths. I'll outline the SLA options.
[02:56] Ravi Patel: Pricing — we're sensitive to unit cost in the nightly batch. Can you show the impact of quantization and batching on cost-per-token?
[03:03] Samir Rao: Yep, we'll run cost-per-1k for float32 vs int8 quant and show batching gains at various QPS. For the nightly batch you get big wins with increased batch sizes.
[03:17] Nora Jennings: On the co-sell side, we want clarity on lead routing and reference credits. How do you usually structure partner referral economics?
[03:24] Lena Ortiz: Typically we offer a co-sell commission or referral credit on first-year revenue plus joint-marketing support. For strategic partners we also do joint case studies and intro credits for pilots. Maya will send a sample one-pager.
[03:36] Maya Chen: I'll include sample contract language in the one-pager so your legal can review.
[03:40] Marcus Lee: One more technical — model fallbacks. If capacity constrained, how do you guarantee throughput?
[03:45] Samir Rao: Smart routing. We can fall back to a lower-cost variant or region-based routing. For mission-critical flows we recommend Dedicated with burst capacity and autoscale rules. We'll show latency delta between variants.
[03:58] [05:00] (cross talk, link dropped briefly)
[05:10] Maya Chen: Sorry — we lost a second. Back. Nora, are there three pilots you want prioritized?
[05:17] Nora Jennings: Yes — 1) Clinical summarization pilot (highest priority), 2) Patient intake triage (real-time, lower QPS but low latency), 3) Back-office nightly ETL synth (batch 32k). The first two are product-critical.
[05:30] Maya Chen: Confirmed. That helps for capacity planning. For the clinical summarization, any PHI restrictions?
[05:36] Ravi Patel: PHI will be present; for that one we need Private or a HIPAA BA. Can you support HIPAA BAA for hosted?
[05:44] Lena Ortiz: We do offer BAAs for Dedicated and Private; hosted can be covered under enterprise agreements depending on control plane requirements. I'll flag legal but it is doable.
[05:56] Nora Jennings: Ok good. Procurement timeline — we aim to sign pilot agreements by mid-April.
[06:02] Maya Chen: We'll align perf numbers and the co-sell terms timeline to that.
[06:07] Samir Rao: Technical detail I'll include in the perf runs: model size, quant levels, GPU types (p4/rtx/future H-series), inference kernels, peak memory, and KV-cache hit assumptions. For the nightly ETL I'll show compute hours and an estimated monthly token bill.
[06:25] Marcus Lee: Are there any known regressions with 32k context on your current kernels? We had trouble with some open-source runtimes.
[06:32] Samir Rao: We optimized attention to handle 32k reasonably; there are throughput vs latency tradeoffs. We'll present p50/p95/p99 and memory footprints. Expect higher per-token cost in extreme long context but caching can mitigate some of it for repeated prefixes.
[06:48] Nora Jennings: Can you share a sample benchmark spreadsheet format?
[06:52] Maya Chen: Yes, Samir will upload the raw sheet and a sanitized summary. We'll also include a short explanation of each column.
[06:58] Ravi Patel: On security again — SSO integration. We use Okta. Will you support SAML/SCIM for user provisioning in the console?
[07:06] Lena Ortiz: Yes, we support SAML and SCIM for RBAC. For Private we can integrate with your IdP directly.
[07:13] Marcus Lee: Audit logs and event retention — what's the default?
[07:17] Maya Chen: Default retention is 90 days; extended retention is available as an add-on. We'll include audit log format in the security pack.
[07:26] Nora Jennings: Great. Anything else from Redwood?
[07:29] Samir Rao: One ask — could you share a representative query mix and peak concurrency numbers? Helps us pick default batch sizes and instance types.
[07:36] Ravi Patel: I'll export last 3 weeks of anonymized telemetry and send to Samir. Should be able to by Tuesday.
[07:43] Maya Chen: Awesome. For co-sell mechanics, Nora — do you want Redwood to handle initial outreach to your named health systems, or prefer intros?
[07:50] Nora Jennings: We prefer joint intro for top targets, and Redwood-led outreach for the rest. We also want a simple referral tracking sheet.
[07:58] Lena Ortiz: We'll provide a tracking spreadsheet and set a cadence for win-back reporting.
[08:03] [08:20] (background noise)
[08:25] Maya Chen: Perfect. Let's recap next steps — Samir runs perf by 3/26, Maya sends co-sell one-pager 3/23, Lena shares references 3/25, Ravi provides telemetry and SLA targets 3/24.
[08:40] Nora Jennings: One small ask — exemplars for anonymized PHI handling so our compliance folks can see the redaction approach.
[08:47] Lena Ortiz: We'll include redaction patterns and dataflow diagrams in the security pack.
[08:52] Marcus Lee: If everything looks good, we'll propose a pilot SOW for the clinical summarization first. Estimated budget TBD after perf numbers.
[08:59] Maya Chen: Understood. Any blockers on Redwood side?
[09:02] Samir Rao: None — just need the telemetry and acceptance criteria for latency.
[09:06] Ravi Patel: We'll send acceptance criteria — target p95 under 450ms for real-time flows.
[09:12] Samir Rao: Noted. We'll design runs to show p95 and p99.
[09:16] (brief pause)
[09:20] Maya Chen: Alright, last thing — do you want a joint exec briefing next week to align stakeholders?
[09:25] Nora Jennings: Yes, that would help. Could be 30 minutes.
[09:29] Maya Chen: I'll propose times after the sheet is ready.
[09:32] (wrap-up)

Recap (end of call):
- Prioritized pilots: Clinical summarization (PHI, high priority), Patient triage (real-time), Nightly ETL (batch 32k).
- Perf plan: Samir to deliver hosted vs dedicated benchmarks (8k/32k, cold vs warm, batching) by 2026-03-26.
- Security: Redwood to share security pack including SOC2, KMS options, SAML/SCIM integration, audit log format, and PHI redaction notes.
- Co-sell: Redwood to share one-pager with referral/credit terms; agreed joint intros for top targets.
- Next meeting: Exec alignment 30-min (TBD) after perf sheet.

Links shared during call: https://redwood.internal/co-sell-one-pager (placeholder), https://redwood.internal/security-pack (placeholder), perf-sheet-template.xlsx (placeholder)

End of transcript.
file_notes: Pilot prioritization call — partner handoff style; contains PHI/BAA discussion and performance benchmarking commitments. Transcription contains a few dropped words and minor speaker attribution noise as is typical.
